response.title: Harborlight FY2027 Budget Drive-In Brief

segments.heading: The main ask
segments.text: Staff ask the board to approve an FY2027 budget of $1,610,000. The money would open a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library. It would also add two site coordinators. Staff estimate the new site would serve 180 more learners a year. They also say it would cut the waitlist in half. The board agreed to vote on the FY2027 budget on October 21.

segments.heading: Who Harborlight served
segments.text: Harborlight enrolled 1,148 adult learners in fiscal year 2026. They attended five neighborhood sites. The year before, the count was 936. Of those learners, 412 were working toward a high school equivalency credential. And 389 were English language learners. The results were strong. Sixty-eight percent of learners who stayed at least 12 weeks gained one or more reading levels on the CASAS assessment. Seventy-one learners earned a high school equivalency credential. No year in the organization's history has seen more.

segments.heading: The people behind it
segments.text: Volunteers carry much of the load. A corps of 214 volunteer tutors gave 9,870 tutoring hours. On average, a tutor stayed 14 months. Harborlight also employs 11 full-time staff. Four of them are site coordinators. A learner at the Riverside site shared what this work means. In the learner's words: "I read my granddaughter a bedtime story for the first time this spring."

segments.heading: Where the money went
segments.text: Here is how the FY2026 budget looked. Operating expenses came to $1,420,000. Program costs made up 81 percent of spending. Foundation grants brought in $640,000. Individual donors gave $388,000. The city's adult education contract paid $295,000. The cost per learner was $1,237. The treasurer flagged one concern. Reserves stand at 3.2 months of operating expenses. The board's target is 4 months, so reserves fall short.

segments.heading: Too many people waiting
segments.text: More adults want classes than Harborlight has room for. When the year ended, 287 adults were still on the waitlist. Most of them were waiting at the Eastgate and Riverside sites. On average, a person waited nine weeks. The proposed sixth site would open at the Eastgate branch library. Staff estimate the new site would cut the waitlist in half.

segments.heading: The board's requests
segments.text: The board held a retreat on September 13. There, members asked staff for two things. The first is a one-page summary of the FY2027 budget request. Staff are to bring that summary to the board meeting on October 21. The second is a short deck. Board members want to use it with funders when they talk about the sixth site.

response.recap: Keep three things in mind. First, staff ask for an FY2027 budget of $1,610,000. It would add a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library and two site coordinators. Second, 287 adults were on the waitlist at year end, and the average wait was nine weeks. Third, reserves stand at 3.2 months, below the board's target of 4 months.
